workshop.verify_both_storefront_actions_work_agai: Verify availability and delivery catalog views show live results for all three products. Allow in-flight requests to finish and, if needed, one 5-second breaker cooldown.
workshop.in_network_faults_click_clear_all_faults: In Network Faults, click “Clear all faults” in the Fault injection tab. Then open “Fallbacks & timeouts” and click “Restore default settings”. workshop.how_to_restore_default_behavior_after_an: How to restore default behavior after an experiment
workshop.blast_radius_means_which_customer_action: Blast radius is the impact beyond the faulty lamp: catalog failure, chair/desk queue time or rejected requests. An abort condition is an unexpected result at which you clear faults immediately. A fast Shipping disconnect demonstrates catalog error propagation; it need not saturate workers.
workshop.the_period_you_measure_in_each_phase_use: The period you measure in each phase. Use comparable fresh windows, such as 60–90 seconds. Grafana uses one-minute rates, so allow the previous phase to leave the calculation before interpreting a new phase.
workshop.the_charts_you_read_during_the_experimen: The charts you read during the experiment. “Customer-facing p95 latency” shows a response-time estimate that 95% of requests fall at or below; “Dependency p95 latency” helps identify the slow provider. A chart in seconds uses 1.5 s for 1500 ms.
workshop.the_measurement_collector_it_asks_the_se: The measurement collector. It asks the services for their counters and timing measurements every five seconds, stores those time series, and supplies data to Grafana. Its website lets you inspect raw measurements or run queries; the guided tasks do not require you to type queries there.
workshop.the_useful_response_storefront_returns_w: An honest replacement for a missing dependency result. Inventory says “Stock unconfirmed” and disables the lamp’s availability action; Shipping leaves the quote unavailable. Enabling a fallback also enables a per-product/dependency circuit breaker: after a failed call it skips that path for 5 seconds, then allows one probe. Timeout, breaker and fallback have separate jobs.
workshop.how_long_storefront_will_wait_for_a_depe: How long an admitted request waits for a dependency. A short timeout releases shared capacity sooner. The worker queue has its own 1000 ms limit; shortening dependency timeouts alone does not provide a useful response.
workshop.the_problem_you_introduce_in_network_fau: The problem you introduce in Network Faults: a slower reply or a disconnected dependency. It affects the real local request path.
workshop.your_measurements_with_normal_service_be: Your measurements with normal service, before you inject a fault. Compare later runs against these numbers.
workshop.what_do_baseline_timeout_fallback_and_th: What do baseline, timeout, fallback, and the monitoring tools mean?
workshop.settings_apply_immediately_on_windows_an: Settings apply to new requests immediately. A short timeout frees shared workers, the breaker pauses repeated failed calls, and the fallback keeps other products visible without inventing data. Keep the exact same fault and traffic for the retest. After cleanup, allow up to one 5-second cooldown for live data to return.
workshop.optional_api_and_terminal_examples_the_w: Optional API and terminal examples. The workshop can be completed with the browser controls.
workshop.collects_service_metrics_every_five_seco: Collects service metrics every five seconds and supplies Grafana. Optional for raw queries; no input needed for the guided challenges.
workshop.read_charts_of_response_times_failures_a: Read charts of response times, failures, and fallback use.
workshop.inject_a_fault_then_use_the_fallbacks_ti: Inject a fault, then use the Fallbacks & timeouts tab to enable a mitigation. All controls work on Windows and Mac.
workshop.network_faults_create_the_problem_and_te: Network Faults · create the problem and test a response
workshop.click_check_availability_and_order_previ: Click Check availability and Order preview; read the result and request time.
workshop.windows_start_bat_stop_bat_mac_start_com: Windows: start.bat / stop.bat · Mac: start.command / stop.command. In a source checkout, these files are at the repository root.
workshop.use_storefront_network_faults_and_grafan: Use Storefront, Network Faults, and Grafana. Fill the notes with your own results; “Submit notes” reveals an example and unlocks the next challenge.
workshop.open_challenge_1_in_the_sidebar_its_brie: Open Challenge 1 in the sidebar. Its brief explains what to reproduce, why it matters, and the five actions to take.
workshop.extract_the_zip_start_docker_desktop_the: Extract the ZIP, start Docker Desktop, then double-click start.bat (Windows) or start.command (Mac).
workshop.for_each_experiment_compare_three_runs_o: For each experiment, compare three runs of the same customer action: normal service → fault active → the same fault with a mitigation. A mitigation changes how the shop handles the problem. Finish by removing the fault and restoring normal settings.
workshop.the_shop_normally_starts_healthy_in_chal: The shop normally starts healthy. In Challenges 1, 2, and 4, you deliberately add a local network fault to reproduce a customer problem. In Challenge 3, a facilitator or teammate adds a hidden fault for you to investigate. Opening a challenge or submitting answers does not change the running shop.
workshop.you_are_the_engineer_responsible_for_a_l: You are responsible for a three-product shop: Desk Lamp, Task Chair and Writing Desk. All three share Inventory and Shipping services and a Storefront with two workers. A fault targets the lamp’s network branch, while the chair and desk keep healthy dependency paths.
workshop.make_a_working_shop_fail_then_improve_it: Contain one product’s fault before it disrupts the catalog
workshop.investigate_a_small_storefront_through_f: Follow a fault from one product into shared capacity and the complete catalog. Compare the same incident before and after containment.
workshop.browser_storage_is_unavailable_download_: Browser storage is unavailable. Download your notes before leaving.

catalog.title: Three products. One shared shop.
catalog.description: Desk Lamp, Task Chair and Writing Desk use the same Inventory and Shipping services and share two Storefront workers. Network Faults targets only the lamp’s network paths. Under the supplied traffic, a slow lamp can fill the workers and make healthy products wait or fail. A missing lamp result also prevents the complete catalog from being returned.
catalog.loading: Refreshing the catalog… Previous cards, if shown, are from the last completed refresh.
catalog.explanation: Watch the healthy chair and desk, not just the lamp. Inventory fallback disables the lamp’s availability action instead of guessing stock. Shipping fallback leaves its quote unavailable. The short timeout releases a worker; a circuit breaker pauses failed product/dependency calls for 5 seconds, then allows one recovery probe. Clearing faults may need one cooldown before live data returns. Rejected counts are cumulative; compare changes over equal windows. The start launcher supplies fixed background traffic.
catalog.connection_error: Could not refresh the catalog. No current live result is shown.
catalog.capacity_error: All shared workers are busy and the queue limit was reached. Healthy products can be affected too.
catalog.catalog_error: One product could not be confirmed, so this complete catalog response failed. Compare the availability and delivery views, then repeat the same fault after mitigation.
